title: Create test streams with cloud encoding
lead: These optional workflows test the Encoding API. Player experiments using local media or public reference streams do not require a cloud encoder.

blocks.text: Before running a cloud workflow

blocks.title: Starting an encoding incurs charges
blocks.text: A real encoding creates resources in your account and incurs charges. Storage and delivery charges can continue after a VOD encoding finishes. Confirm that live encoders stop. The start, ingest, and stop commands below are instructions to run in your own account.

The shell workflows require Bitmovin CLI 0.7.0, jq, and envsubst from GNU gettext. First-use S3 output creation and Per-Title use Python 3.10 or later with OpenSSL and the pinned Python SDK. The SDK version checked in the public documentation is 1.284.0.

npm install -g @bitmovin/cli@0.7.0
python3 -m venv encoding/.venv
. encoding/.venv/bin/activate
python3 -m pip install -r encoding/requirements.txt
bitmovin --version
python3 -m pip show bitmovin-api-sdk

Keep the secret API key, S3 bucket details, and credentials in the untracked root .env file. Public encoding structure and the input catalog belong in config/encoding.conf. Settings take precedence in this order: shell environment, .env, then config/encoding.conf. Do not commit real account IDs, deployment URLs, or credentials.

S3 outputs are resolved by an exact BITMOVIN_OUTPUT_NAME match and created only when none exists. Multiple matches stop the workflow. Bootstrap the output once before running workflows concurrently. The shell workflows also accept OUTPUT_ID for an existing output and INPUT_ID for an existing HTTPS input. The Per-Title script accepts OUTPUT_ID as well.

The included templates specify PUBLIC_READ for output. Prepare an S3 configuration that permits those writes and a delivery URL the browser can fetch. For private storage or another delivery arrangement, adjust output permissions and delivery settings.

When working across organizations, the shell workflows use the organization selected in Bitmovin CLI; Per-Title Python uses BITMOVIN_TENANT_ORG_ID. Check that both select the intended organization. First-use S3 creation reads credentials from the environment through the SDK, without passing them as command-line arguments.

blocks.text: Input media and durations differ between cloud scenarios. The local fixture's 60-second duration and two-second video segments do not apply to every cloud template.
Create a VOD test stream

DRY_RUN=1 \
  encoding/test-streams/provision.sh vod-baseline

# Starts a billable one-shot encoding.
encoding/test-streams/provision.sh vod-baseline

The first command resolves existing resources and validates the template without creating resources or starting an encoding. It may still contact account-listing and validation APIs, so it is not fully offline. Missing inputs or outputs use a validation-only placeholder ID. A real run never starts an encoding with that placeholder.

A real run monitors the encoding until FINISHED and prints HLS and DASH URLs. Changing the scenario name selects its template. The multi-audio scenario does not generate DASH, so use the HLS output it actually creates.
To use your output in feature tests, set the common base URL in the shell that starts the test runner, without a trailing slash. This is separate from the application's VITE_VOD_* settings.

export VITE_TEST_STREAM_BASE_URL=\
"https://media.example.test/test-streams"
pnpm --filter @showcase/e2e e2e \
  specs/provisioned-vod.spec.ts --retries=0

The domain above is a placeholder to replace. Tests append expected paths such as vod-baseline/. If configuration is missing, they report it before playback instead of silently substituting other public media.
Adding thumbnails, audio, and subtitles

items: Keep sprite filenames consistent with WebVTT references. The templates use sprite-%number%.jpg to write files such as sprite-0.jpg. An unnumbered filename can disagree with the WebVTT reference and cause image requests to fail.

Multiple bitrates of the same audio are quality choices. Selectable tracks, such as different languages, need distinct language/name metadata and an HLS audio group. A language label alone does not establish a translated soundtrack.
SubRip .srt subtitle files differ from the SRT streaming input protocol. Convert subtitles to WebVTT. A sidecar copies a file unchanged; it does not convert the format.
The included Sintel subtitles are shifted approximately 106.25 seconds earlier so cues appear within a short clip. Tests use the Player's subtitleTracks loading path.
I-frame-only playlists are outside the included templates. A normal HLS master playlist or thumbnail preview does not establish that this feature is present.

blocks.text: Per-Title with three codecs

Per-Title creates quality ladders from content-specific analysis. This example creates independent H.264, HEVC, and AV1 jobs and starts and monitors them with a fixed concurrency of three. One AAC track at 128 kbit/s is created in the H.264 job and shared by HLS and DASH. Fragmented MP4 segments are configured for four seconds.

DRY_RUN=1 python3 \
  encoding/vod-multicodec-pertitle/multicodec_pertitle.py

# Starts three billable encodings and two manifests.
python3 \
  encoding/vod-multicodec-pertitle/multicodec_pertitle.py
This Python script's DRY_RUN prints the resolved plan to standard output and exits before any API call. This differs from the shell workflows' DRY_RUN. It does not produce a dedicated plan JSON file.

A real run waits for every encoding to finish, lists the generated fragmented MP4 outputs, and builds combined manifests using their actual IDs and output paths. Per-Title rendition counts and IDs become available after encoding, so they are not hard-coded in advance. Output is written under test-streams/vod-multicodec-pertitle/<RUN>/, with manifest.mpd and master.m3u8.

Set the input through SOURCE_VOD_MULTICODEC_PERTITLE_HOST and SOURCE_VOD_MULTICODEC_PERTITLE_PATH. There are no GUI controls or command-line flags for minimum/maximum bitrate or fixed-resolution anchors. Adding them requires editing each job's SDK configuration. Concurrency is not automatically adjusted to RAM or content complexity. Check runtime and charges, including AV1, with a short input first.
Start and stop Live DVR

The live-dvr template configures RTMP ingest, 720p/480p/240p video, AAC audio, four-second segments, and a 300-second rewind window. It sets the DASH live-edge offset to 90 seconds. Point local VITE_LIVE_HLS_URL and VITE_LIVE_DASH_URL settings at the channel while it is running if needed.

DRY_RUN=1 encoding/live-dvr/start.sh

# Starts a billable live encoder.
encoding/live-dvr/start.sh

Once the encoder is RUNNING, send ingest to the encoder IP shown by the workflow. The following test pattern stops sending after 420 seconds. Replace the IP placeholder with the result from your own run.

ffmpeg -re \
  -f lavfi -i testsrc2=size=1280x720:rate=30 \
  -f lavfi -i sine=frequency=1000 \
  -c:v libx264 -preset veryfast \
  -tune zerolatency -b:v 3M -g 60 \
  -c:a aac -b:a 128k -t 420 \
  -f flv "rtmp://<encoderIp>/live/dvrshowcase"

After enough media has arrived to fill 300 seconds, check the manifest's rewind window and the Player's values. The template also configures automatic shutdown if no stream arrives within ten minutes of startup or ingest bytes stop for 30 seconds. Ending ingest does not replace checking that the encoder stopped.

bitmovin encoding jobs stop <encoding-id>
bitmovin encoding jobs status <encoding-id>

blocks.title: Ending monitoring does not stop the encoder
blocks.text: The shell scripts stop monitoring after repeated unreadable statuses. That does not establish that the cloud job stopped. Check the displayed encoding ID and stop the job if needed. If one Per-Title job fails, check the other jobs' states separately.
